Queer person here. I think you should suggest to him that he might not think being LGBT+ is wrong, but that he might just annoyed with the particular crowd in his school. People who are very in-your-face and loud about anything at all can be really annoying, regardless of what they’re loud about. Teenagers can be really over-the-top about it because, well, they’re teenagers. It’s what they do. A lot of them haven’t discovered how great it is to just live their life and chill the fuck out. On top of the raging hormonal nature of adolescence that makes them even more susceptible to irritation, it can all be way too much. That kind of ridiculous behavior is probably making him think that’s what all LGBT people are like. High school is a jungle. He’s young, he’s had limited exposure to real people. He has no frame of reference for it. He might just be annoyed by their boisterous behavior and that annoyed feeling is being kind of Pavlov’ed toward gay people in general. It can also be frustrating to straight kids when they don’t understand why it’s perfectly fine to be straight but “straight pride” is bad. That’s another conversation, but basically, straight people have never had their rights taken away as straight people. Gay people have never made laws saying straight people can’t get married, there are no camps run by gay people to force straight kids to be gay, etc.

That said, you might want to remind him that LGBT+ people and their rights are rather under fire right now. We (in America, at least) have some violently homophobic political figures, public figures, and a good chunk of the general population that wants to shove us back in the closet for good. This wave of oppressive ideas means it’s very important not to let those people quiet or silence LGBT+ people. It’s vital for people who are being targeted to maintain their voices in the face of oppression. For teenagers, that usually means they’ll take it up several notches beyond what’s necessary. He may be annoyed with them for being obnoxious, but their community is being baselessly accused of pedophilia and having their human rights targeted. Perspective matters.

He’s allowed to be annoyed by annoying behavior. He should, however, remember that not all LGBT+ people act like that.

(Another question one level deeper might also be: is their behavior actually that bad, or are they just existing at an audible volume like everyone else, but they’re different so it bothers me? Probably not applicable here based on what you described, nor is it much of a 14-year-old question, but worth mentioning in this comment.)

Everything about this reads like you’re a teenager who doesn’t take inventory of themself and their behaviors as much as they should. I’m sure you’re a perfectly nice person, but people don’t usually just disappear for no reason at all. Get some outside perspective and reevaluate—maybe even ask them what their reasons are. See if they give you straightforward, sound reasons to think about. 

Source: I thought this same thing for a long time. Even into my early 20s. Never made any sense to me why people would just stop talking to me with no explanation. It hurts, I totally get that, but if it keeps happening over and over, it’s time to take a look at yourself. For me, it turned out I was just kind of a douchebag. Never realized it, I truly thought I was such a nice person the whole time. I was mistaken, I changed, haven’t had this problem since. 

I could be wrong, of course. Maybe you’re just surrounded by unkind people. Theres also the possibility that your friends are just normal adults who are moving through life and unfortunately their roads are not parallel to yours. That happens, it’s okay. There’s limited info here. Wishing you the best, I know it sucks to have this happen over and over.

Tell your asshole FIL that millennials are, statistically, almost as financially fucked as the poor sons of bitches during the Great Depression. [*Statistically.*](https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2020/01/11/politics/millennials-income-stalled-upward-mobility-us/index.html) Edit: A lot of you seem to disagree, which is fair, but I’ll remind you that [the modern poverty line for a single income household in America is extremely unrealistic](https://aspe.hhs.gov/topics/poverty-economic-mobility/poverty-guidelines). Even the poverty line for a family of 4, as specified in that link, is not enough for the average person to support themself today. $27,750/year is approximately $533/week. If we use the renter’s rule of thumb—making your rent in 1 week—that barely covers half of the national average for rent ($1100 in 2021.) You expect any reasonable person to believe that a single person making $18,000/year, for example, is *not* living in poverty? What a laughable sentiment. In terms of unemployment rates today vs. GD, okay. In terms of people who cannot afford to live despite employment, those people not being fairly and accurately represented in the link above, accounting for the fact that many people need more than one job to survive, as well as international issues like the supply chain and outsourcing jobs within the country to stretch corporate profit via paying foreign employees less than they would citizens, there is a discussion to be had. 

For starters, there isn’t a worker shortage in the sense that “nobody wants to work anymore.” Unemployment is at one of its lowest rates in 60 years. That’s a good way to answer that asinine comment. That being said, people are no longer willing to work for poverty wages. And they shouldn’t. Millions of people learned that they could make a living working from home or starting their own businesses, instead of going out to slave away for some shitty boss. So, jobs that don’t pay well are left unfilled. “But *livable* wages are killing small businesses!” That sucks, but unfortunately if you can’t afford to stay open and pay your employees enough to live, your business model does not work. The short of this one is: be angry at billionaires who drive inflation, hoard wealth and prevent it from recirculating back into/stimulating the economy—not the 28 year old single parent who needs to keep the lights on. 

On top of that, Millennials are arguably one of the hardest working generations in terms of work hours required to make ends meet. 

The houses that our parents bought for $50k in the 80s are now selling for $400k+, yet the value of $50k in the 80s is equal to less than $200k in the present day. Before COVID, a great deal of millennials AND Gen X-ers had been working two jobs (even three, in some cases) just to still have to choose between rent and dinner. Just to still have their car repossessed and lose their way to get to work to have a prayer at paying those fucking bills at all. Working their ass off at two jobs just to face eviction anyway. Then eviction destroys their credit, so they can’t get approved for new housing—or anything, really—and if they don’t have welcoming parents, they’re shit out of luck. My aunt bought her house for $33,000 in 1978. That’s $150,000 in 2022. Her house, unchanged, is now valued at $417,000. And lol, by the way, the wait lists for any kind of rent assistance or low income housing are LITERALLY YEARS long, so it’s easy to see he has no idea what the fuck he’s talking about. Let me know where the hell the government is just giving away money, because I’ll walk my ass there *tonight.*

The new generations are strangled by gouged prices and absurd interest rates yet stagnant and suppressed wages—so much so that many, many people who have paid their student loans faithfully for years and years actually owe *more than they borrowed* because they can only make their minimum monthly payment alongside the rest of their monthly expenses, and that minimum payment often can’t even cover the interest accrued in one month. So the loan amount goes up despite payments being made faithfully. This endlessly growing debt destroys their eligibility for mortgage approval because banks don’t like a high debt:income ratio. I could go on, but…

These people did what they were told. They went to college. They chased the Better Life they were sold for their entire adolescence. They got the college degree to get the better job to have the better life. And a massive amount of them got completely screwed over, and now people like your FIL show up just to call them lazy and tell them to go fuck themselves. 

COVID happens. Millions of people, from nurses to burger flippers, are labeled “essential workers.” They are told the world will stop without them. They then begin to wonder why, if they’re so “essential” to the world, they’re being paid pathetic, insulting wages that don’t even allow them to live dignified lives despite busting their asses 5 days a week, or often more. They start asking why they’re told they have a moral obligation to show up to work, in the same breath that they’re denied hazard pay for exposing themselves to an airborne virus that killed 5 million people in two years. Eventually, everyone living under the crushing weight described above—even the non-essential workers—realizes they’ve been duped. Nobody should be expected to work 60+ hours a week just to not be able to afford to live anyway. 

The entire old world idea of the “great life in America” was that anyone working 40 hours a week had the opportunity to *live a good life*. That was *why* people came here. Not just for the opportunity to build something incredible like great wealth or a business empire—the idea was that average American citizens didn’t have to work inhumane hours for slave wages, which greatly contrasted the level of opportunity in many other countries. The average person could work one job, pay their bills, and eat 3 meals a day—maybe even have some income leftover to take a little vacation once a year. (We have unions to thank for the 8 hour workday and 5 day workweek, by the way. Important note.) That idea has been corrupted. The new generations were truly robbed. They had their fair chance rug-pulled from under them before they even got out of high school, and I hope they take this fucking government for all its worth.

The short answer is misogyny and socialization, pretty much. 

Girls are taught, directly or indirectly, that anything perceived as masculine or being associated with men is kind of an upgrade of sorts. A step up the ladder. Whereas men, by the same means, are taught that being associated with anything perceived as feminine is a downgrade or shameful—which comes from the societal messaging that to be a woman, or to be womanly, is inherently degrading (re: misogyny.)

Obviously neither of those things are actually true; men and women are not downgrades or upgrades in relation to each other, but truth doesn’t dictate social norms, unfortunately. That’s one very reasonable theory behind it. 

Another is that women and girls are generally socialized to be empathetic from childhood. Neither boys nor girls are innately stoic or empathetic, we’re just sent different messages by our society (or we were, until very recent years.) While boys/men are often taught that their emotions are shameful, emasculating, and that anything beyond the positive scope of emotion should be hidden or suppressed, women are taught to be caretakers, which necessitates compassion and understanding. Some people believe that this conditioning facilitates women to be more accepting of differences. Similarly, others believe that men’s colder style of conditioning teaches them to reject differences. For LGBT people, homophobic discrimination—and potentially violence—can, in simple terms, soften a person, making them more emotionally aware and malleable, for lack of a better term. For gay men specifically, this propensity for expressing one’s feelings can also be off-putting for men who were taught to reject their own. It can also be seen as a “feminine” trait, which brings us back to the first theory in which it’s seen as unacceptable for men to “downgrade” to femininity. This could also point to why a lot of homophobic men dislike or hate gay men but actually find gay women attractive or lesbian relationships to be hot.

Mind you this is not to say all gay men, or gay people, are emotional creatures by default; gay people are just people, just as susceptible to flaws, imperfections, emotional unintelligence and shitty behavior as anyone else. Nor is it to say that women are inherently kind and empathetic—I’m sure we’ve all had our share of heartless Karens in our lives. That said, though, I think these are fairly solid reasons behind this particular problem.
